texts.text: Weekly Provincial Summary

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Variable rain accumulations were observed in all parts of the province over the past several days. Isolated rainfall resulted in small amounts of precipitation in some areas over the past week with accumulations ranging from 0 mm to 15.6 mm (Table 1). The Pas received the most rain this week with 15.6 mm.

Isolated rainfall resulted in small amounts of precipitation in some areas over the past week with accumulations ranging from 0 mm to 15.6 mm (Table 1). The Pas received the most rain this week with 15.6 mm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to June 15 range from 73.3 mm to 136.8 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Lack of precipitation this season has resulted in the East, Interlake, and large parts of the Northwest having accumulations under 60% of normal. While accumulations in the Southwest and parts of the Central regions are closer to normal, only Virden and Carberry EC have accumulated more than 100% of the 30-year average since May 1.
texts.text: Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to June 15 range from 73.3 mm to 136.8 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Lack of precipitation this season has resulted in the East, Interlake, and large parts of the Northwest having accumulations under 60% of normal. While accumulations in the Southwest and parts of the Central regions are closer to normal, only Virden and Carberry EC have accumulated more than 100% of the 30-year average since May 1.

texts.orig: Forages
texts.text: Forages

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Scattered showers in the Northwest region have provided some much needed moisture to help perk up pastures after dry conditions.
texts.text: Scattered showers in the Northwest region have provided some much needed moisture to help perk up pastures after dry conditions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Alfalfa has started to bloom, and some grasses have begun to head out.
texts.text: Alfalfa has started to bloom, and some grasses have begun to head out.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Most dairies have finished first cut, and a few beef producers have begun first cut. Anticipated yields range from normal to below average.
texts.text: Most dairies have finished first cut, and a few beef producers have begun first cut. Anticipated yields range from normal to below average.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Some producers intend to graze fenced hay fields where possible, and some have begun taking fall rye crops as silage rather than grain as was originally intended.
texts.text: Some producers intend to graze fenced hay fields where possible, and some have begun taking fall rye crops as silage rather than grain as was originally intended.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Corn intended for silage is growing well.
texts.text: Corn intended for silage is growing well.

texts.orig: Livestock
texts.text: Livestock

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Most cattle are out on pasture.
texts.text: Most cattle are out on pasture.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Conditions in much of Manitoba are dry. Pastures are holding for now, but it is becoming increasingly evident that animals will need to be supplemented or removed from current grazing systems as the summer continues.
texts.text: Conditions in much of Manitoba are dry. Pastures are holding for now, but it is becoming increasingly evident that animals will need to be supplemented or removed from current grazing systems as the summer continues.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Black flies are active, causing irritation to cattle on pasture. Producers are encouraged to monitor animal behavior and apply appropriate fly control methods to reduce the impact.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Dugouts are at about 70% capacity if they are not spring fed, which is low for this time of year.

texts.orig: Regional Comments
texts.text: Regional Comments

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With minimal rainfall across the region, crops would benefit from additional moisture at this stage of development. Crops are generally in good condition.
texts.text: With minimal rainfall across the region, crops would benefit from additional moisture at this stage of development. Crops are generally in good condition.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat is moving into the boot stage and fall rye is headed. Spring cereals range from tillering to early stem elongation. Corn is in the V4 to V5 stage.
texts.text: Winter wheat is moving into the boot stage and fall rye is headed. Spring cereals range from tillering to early stem elongation. Corn is in the V4 to V5 stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Late seeded canola fields have emerged. Early seeded fields are in the rosette stage. Flea beetles have been reported, particularly in late-seeded canola. Sunflowers range from emergence to four leaf stage. Flax ranges from first leaves to 5 to 10 cm in height.
texts.text: Late seeded canola fields have emerged. Early seeded fields are in the rosette stage. Flea beetles have been reported, particularly in late-seeded canola. Sunflowers range from emergence to four leaf stage. Flax ranges from first leaves to 5 to 10 cm in height.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybeans range from emergence to third trifoliate stage. Field peas range from 6 to 8 nodes.
texts.text: Soybeans range from emergence to third trifoliate stage. Field peas range from 6 to 8 nodes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In-crop herbicide applications are approximately 60% complete. The majority of early seeded cereals and corn have been sprayed, along with some early-seeded canola.
texts.text: In-crop herbicide applications are approximately 60% complete. The majority of early seeded cereals and corn have been sprayed, along with some early-seeded canola.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Seeding is virtually complete across the region. Herbicide applications are ongoing in various crops as they reach the appropriate stages. Spring cereal and field pea herbicide applications are nearing completion, while herbicide applications in canola and soybeans continue. Windy conditions continue to challenge spray operations.
texts.text: Seeding is virtually complete across the region. Herbicide applications are ongoing in various crops as they reach the appropriate stages. Spring cereal and field pea herbicide applications are nearing completion, while herbicide applications in canola and soybeans continue. Windy conditions continue to challenge spray operations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Some precipitation fell in the Northwest region last week, with The Pas recording the highest amount at 15.6 mm. Some crops are starting to show signs of lack of precipitation, especially in lighter soils. Overnight temperatures were cooler this past week, with Minitonas station recording the lowest overnight temperature of 3.7°C.
texts.text: Manitoba Some precipitation fell in the Northwest region last week, with The Pas recording the highest amount at 15.6 mm. Some crops are starting to show signs of lack of precipitation, especially in lighter soils. Overnight temperatures were cooler this past week, with Minitonas station recording the lowest overnight temperature of 3.7°C.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter wheat are mostly in the flowering stage. Spring wheat is mostly at the tillering stage, with later seeded fields further behind.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat are mostly in the flowering stage. Spring wheat is mostly at the tillering stage, with later seeded fields further behind.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas continue growth in the vegetative stage. Field pea weevil feeding has been noted in many fields. Soybeans are in the V1 to V2 stage and in good condition at this point.
texts.text: Field peas continue growth in the vegetative stage. Field pea weevil feeding has been noted in many fields. Soybeans are in the V1 to V2 stage and in good condition at this point.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola plant growth varies across the region. Earliest seeded fields are at the 6 leaf stage. Dry conditions have led to some stagy canola fields due to some seeds germinating late. Flea beetles continue to be monitored and some extra control has been required in some fields.
texts.text: Canola plant growth varies across the region. Earliest seeded fields are at the 6 leaf stage. Dry conditions have led to some stagy canola fields due to some seeds germinating late. Flea beetles continue to be monitored and some extra control has been required in some fields.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Planting is complete, with producers shifting focus to crop management, particularly herbicide applications and monitoring for pests and diseases. Herbicide applications were made in a timely manner over the past week, due to dry weather across most of the region. Only a few areas in the northwest of the Central region received notable rainfall. Overall, crops appear to be in good condition. Cooler temperatures have supported strong crop establishment and early season growth. Most crops have now recovered from earlier issues such as soil crusting, frost injury and high winds.
texts.text: Planting is complete, with producers shifting focus to crop management, particularly herbicide applications and monitoring for pests and diseases. Herbicide applications were made in a timely manner over the past week, due to dry weather across most of the region. Only a few areas in the northwest of the Central region received notable rainfall. Overall, crops appear to be in good condition. Cooler temperatures have supported strong crop establishment and early season growth. Most crops have now recovered from earlier issues such as soil crusting, frost injury and high winds.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye are advancing quickly. Fall rye is in late anthesis, while winter wheat ranges from booting to heads fully emerged. Spraying for fusarium head blight has begun. Spring cereals are in the stem elongation stage. Herbicide applications are largely complete in spring cereals.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye are advancing quickly. Fall rye is in late anthesis, while winter wheat ranges from booting to heads fully emerged. Spraying for fusarium head blight has begun. Spring cereals are in the stem elongation stage. Herbicide applications are largely complete in spring cereals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Corn ranges from V3 to V6. Most fields have grown past earlier frost damage and emergence issues caused by soil crusting and strong winds. Some fields show minor purpling due to early season phosphorus deficiency.
texts.text: Corn ranges from V3 to V6. Most fields have grown past earlier frost damage and emergence issues caused by soil crusting and strong winds. Some fields show minor purpling due to early season phosphorus deficiency.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola ranges from early rosette to bolting. The first flowers have appeared in the earliest fields. Herbicide applications are complete for the most advanced fields but continue in later seeded fields. Sunflowers are in the V8 to V10 stage. Flax is at the 8 to 10 true leaf stage, with the start of leaf spiral.
texts.text: Canola ranges from early rosette to bolting. The first flowers have appeared in the earliest fields. Herbicide applications are complete for the most advanced fields but continue in later seeded fields. Sunflowers are in the V8 to V10 stage. Flax is at the 8 to 10 true leaf stage, with the start of leaf spiral.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Field peas range from V5 to V10. Pea weevil feeding is being reported in many fields, particularly in the west of the Central region. The most advanced soybeans are in the 3 rd trifoliate stage. Most first pass herbicide applications are complete. Minor cases of iron deficiency chlorosis are present.
texts.text: Field peas range from V5 to V10. Pea weevil feeding is being reported in many fields, particularly in the west of the Central region. The most advanced soybeans are in the 3 rd trifoliate stage. Most first pass herbicide applications are complete. Minor cases of iron deficiency chlorosis are present.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall accumulations ranged from 0 mm to 4.4 mm across the region with more needed. Winter cereals continue to develop well. On average, spring cereals are at the beginning of the stem elongation stage. Herbicide applications in spring cereals are estimated as complete.
texts.text: Rainfall accumulations ranged from 0 mm to 4.4 mm across the region with more needed. Winter cereals continue to develop well. On average, spring cereals are at the beginning of the stem elongation stage. Herbicide applications in spring cereals are estimated as complete.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Corn is in the V3 to V5 stage and is growing well. First herbicide applications are complete across the region. Second pass of herbicide is planned for most acres.
texts.text: Corn is in the V3 to V5 stage and is growing well. First herbicide applications are complete across the region. Second pass of herbicide is planned for most acres.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Canola ranges from the four leaf stage to early bolting. With a month long seeding window there is a wide range of crop development across the region. Herbicide application is ongoing with the earlier planted fields finished and mid to late planted acres yet to be covered.
texts.text: Manitoba Canola ranges from the four leaf stage to early bolting. With a month long seeding window there is a wide range of crop development across the region. Herbicide application is ongoing with the earlier planted fields finished and mid to late planted acres yet to be covered.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Soybean crop stage varies. Some late seeded fields are emerging while others are in the 3 rd trifoliate. The majority of fields have had first pass herbicide application. Some iron deficiency chlorosis has been noted. Field peas are in the V5 to V8 stage.
texts.text: Soybean crop stage varies. Some late seeded fields are emerging while others are in the 3 rd trifoliate. The majority of fields have had first pass herbicide application. Some iron deficiency chlorosis has been noted. Field peas are in the V5 to V8 stage.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Interlake region received limited amounts of rainfall over the past week. Soils are becoming drier and timely moisture is needed to maintain crop condition and fill out plant stands. Growth has been rapid over the past week in many crops. Strong winds continue to be a concern, interfering with spraying operations, damaging crop stands and drying out the soil surface.
texts.text: The Interlake region received limited amounts of rainfall over the past week. Soils are becoming drier and timely moisture is needed to maintain crop condition and fill out plant stands. Growth has been rapid over the past week in many crops. Strong winds continue to be a concern, interfering with spraying operations, damaging crop stands and drying out the soil surface.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye has headed and is flowering. Winter wheat is at the head emergence stage. Spring cereals range from tillering to stem elongation. The majority of spring wheat has had herbicides applied. Corn ranges from V3 to V5, and the majority has had a first herbicide application.
texts.text: Fall rye has headed and is flowering. Winter wheat is at the head emergence stage. Spring cereals range from tillering to stem elongation. The majority of spring wheat has had herbicides applied. Corn ranges from V3 to V5, and the majority has had a first herbicide application.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola ranges from emerging to the 4 leaf stage. Some fields have uneven stands due to flea beetle damage and dry conditions. Some canola reseeding due to soil crusting, poor emergence, flea beetle and wind damage, but is not widespread.
texts.text: Canola ranges from emerging to the 4 leaf stage. Some fields have uneven stands due to flea beetle damage and dry conditions. Some canola reseeding due to soil crusting, poor emergence, flea beetle and wind damage, but is not widespread.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Sunflowers are in the 2 to 4 leaf stage, and most have received herbicides. Flax has emerged and the stands look good. Growth stages range from cotyledon to the 8 leaf stage.
texts.text: Sunflowers are in the 2 to 4 leaf stage, and most have received herbicides. Flax has emerged and the stands look good. Growth stages range from cotyledon to the 8 leaf stage.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Peas are in the 4 to 6 node stage. Soybeans are as advanced as 3 rd trifoliate. Some iron deficiency chlorosis noted. Herbicide applications are nearing completion.
texts.text: Peas are in the 4 to 6 node stage. Soybeans are as advanced as 3 rd trifoliate. Some iron deficiency chlorosis noted. Herbicide applications are nearing completion.
